stem: The student wants to describe the method Raman used in her study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Ecologist Priya Raman studied dragonflies in Montana's Bitterroot Valley.
• She asked whether ponds created by beaver dams support more dragonfly species than nearby stream reaches without dams.
• Over two summers, her team netted adult dragonflies along 40 transects, half at beaver ponds and half along undammed stretches of stream.
• Beaver-pond transects averaged 14 dragonfly species; undammed transects averaged 8.
• Raman concluded that beavers indirectly boost insect diversity by creating still water.
choices: Comparing transects at beaver ponds and undammed stretches, Raman found an average of 14 dragonfly species at the ponds versus 8 elsewhere.
Over two summers, Raman's team netted adult dragonflies along 40 transects, half at beaver ponds and half along undammed stretches of stream.
Raman asked whether ponds created by beaver dams support more dragonfly species than do nearby stream reaches that lack dams.
Raman concluded that by creating still water, beavers indirectly increase the diversity of the dragonflies living in the valley.
explanation: The goal asks for the study's method, meaning how the data were collected. Choice B's main clause gives exactly that: the team netted adult dragonflies along 40 transects over two summers, split between beaver ponds and undammed streams. It is the only choice whose main point is the procedure.

A.why: You saw the method words in the opening phrase ("comparing transects") and stopped there. The main clause of this sentence reports the result, 14 species versus 8. The method is only tucked into a side phrase, and the goal needs it to be the main point.

C.why: This is the study's question, not its method. You may have taken the comparison it sets up for a description of the procedure, but nothing here tells how Raman collected her data.

D.why: This sentence is accurate to the notes, but it gives Raman's conclusion, which is the last stage of the study, not the method. It's true, but it doesn't do the job the goal asks for.

stem: The student wants to describe the leaves of the most abundant plant species at the Kettle Ridge site. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Kettle Ridge fossil bed in Oregon preserves plants from about 34 million years ago.
• Paleobotanists have described three new species from the site.
• Quercus prima, an oak, had leaves with deeply lobed margins.
• Alnus vetusta, an alder, had leaves with finely double-toothed edges; more than 600 specimens have been recovered, making it the site's most abundant species.
• Ginkgo kettlensis, named for the ridge, had fan-shaped leaves split by a single central notch.
choices: Of the three new species found at Kettle Ridge, one had lobed leaves, one had toothed leaves, and one had fan-shaped leaves.
With more than 600 specimens recovered so far, Alnus vetusta is the most abundant plant species at the Kettle Ridge fossil bed.
Alnus vetusta, the most abundant species at the Kettle Ridge site, had leaves with fine edges that were double-toothed.
Ginkgo kettlensis, named for the ridge where it was found, had fan-shaped leaves that were split by a single central notch.
explanation: The goal has two steps. First, work out which species is most abundant (Alnus vetusta). Then describe its leaves. Choice C names Alnus vetusta, identifies it as the most abundant species, and uses its main clause to describe its finely double-toothed leaves.

A.why: This sentence covers the whole collection instead of zooming in on one member. It never says which leaf type belongs to the most abundant species, so a reader can't tell what that species' leaves looked like.

B.why: This is the subtype trap. It names the right species, but it describes how abundant the species is, not what its leaves looked like. The goal's restriction is the leaves.

D.why: This describes leaves, but they belong to the wrong species. Ginkgo kettlensis isn't the most abundant plant at the site. You matched the word "leaves" without first working out which species the goal points to.

stem: The student wants to explain how Prairie Ember got its name. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Prairie Ember is a red winter wheat released in 2021 by Canada's Northfield Agricultural Station.
• Breeder Tomasz Wilk developed it over eleven years by crossing a drought-tolerant Turkish landrace with a high-yield Canadian line.
• Wilk named the variety for the deep copper glow its kernels take on as they ripen, which he likened to embers.
• In field trials, it yielded 12% more grain than standard varieties during dry seasons.
• Farmers in three provinces planted it on about 40,000 hectares in its first year.
choices: Named by breeder Tomasz Wilk, Prairie Ember was produced by crossing a drought-tolerant Turkish landrace with a Canadian line.
Prairie Ember, a red winter wheat with copper-colored kernels, yielded 12% more grain than standard varieties in dry seasons.
In its first year, farmers in three Canadian provinces planted the new wheat Prairie Ember on about 40,000 hectares.
Prairie Ember takes its name from the copper glow of its ripening kernels, which reminded breeder Tomasz Wilk of embers.
explanation: The goal ends with "how it got its name," and only one note answers that. Choice D builds its main clause around that note: the variety is named for the copper glow of its ripening kernels, which Wilk likened to embers.

A.why: This is the subtype trap. The naming appears only in an opening phrase ("Named by breeder Tomasz Wilk"), and that phrase says who named it, not why. The main clause is about how the wheat was bred.

B.why: This mentions the copper-colored kernels that inspired the name, so it looks close. But it never links that color to the name, and its main clause is about yield.

C.why: This is accurate, but it describes how widely the wheat was planted in its first year. Nothing in it explains where the name came from.

stem: The student wants to describe what researchers had learned about the Tarrow Fault before the 2023 earthquake. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Tarrow Fault runs about 90 kilometers across New Zealand's South Island.
• In 2015, a team led by seismologist Mere Tane dug trenches across the fault.
• The trenches revealed evidence that the fault had ruptured in three large earthquakes over the past 2,000 years.
• On March 3, 2023, a magnitude 6.8 earthquake struck along the fault.
• Afterward, satellite radar showed that the ground had shifted by up to three meters.
• Aftershocks continued for five months.
choices: Years before the 2023 earthquake, trenching revealed that the Tarrow Fault had ruptured three times in the past 2,000 years.
Satellite radar showed that the 2023 earthquake shifted the ground along the Tarrow Fault by as much as three meters.
The Tarrow Fault, which a 2015 trenching study had examined, produced a magnitude 6.8 earthquake in March 2023.
The Tarrow Fault, a 90-kilometer fault on the South Island, has been studied through both trenching and satellite radar.
explanation: The goal limits you to one time period: what was known before 2023. Choice A's main clause gives a finding from that period, the 2015 trenching evidence of three ruptures in 2,000 years, and it signals the timing with "years before the 2023 earthquake."

B.why: This is the subtype trap. It names the right fault, but the radar finding came after the 2023 earthquake. The goal says "before."

C.why: This mentions the 2015 study, but only in a side clause, and it never says what the study found. The main clause is about the 2023 earthquake itself.

D.why: This stays at the level of the general topic. It mixes research from before and after the quake, and it names methods without saying what anyone learned.

stem: The student wants to describe the source of the red dye in the Marsh coverlet. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Delancey Museum holds four woven coverlets made in Ohio between 1835 and 1860.
• The 1838 Fenwick coverlet pairs indigo-dyed wool with undyed cotton.
• The 1846 Marsh coverlet was woven by Jacob Marsh, a German immigrant who operated a Jacquard loom.
• Its red threads were dyed with madder root that Marsh grew in his own garden.
• The 1859 Coyle coverlet was colored with synthetic aniline purple, the earliest such dye in the collection.
choices: The Marsh coverlet was woven in 1846 by Jacob Marsh, a German immigrant to Ohio who operated a Jacquard loom.
The museum's Ohio coverlets include pieces colored with indigo, with madder root, and with synthetic aniline dye.
The red threads of the 1846 Marsh coverlet were dyed with madder root that its weaver grew in his own garden.
Unlike the Marsh coverlet, the 1859 Coyle coverlet was colored with an early synthetic dye, aniline purple.
explanation: The goal names one item (the Marsh coverlet) and one feature (where its red dye came from). Choice C makes the coverlet's red threads its subject and answers directly: madder root that Marsh grew in his own garden.

A.why: This is the subtype trap. It names the right coverlet but describes the weaver's background and loom instead of the dye. That's the maker's biography, not the feature the goal asks about.

B.why: This covers the whole collection when the goal asks about one member of it. It mentions madder root but never ties it to the Marsh coverlet or its red threads.

D.why: This mentions the Marsh coverlet, but its main clause is about the Coyle coverlet's dye. It contrasts two items, and the goal asked you to describe one detail of one item.
